items.title: Jay McShann interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: But anyway though, we had a lot of fun with Lucky. We used to play a half an hour each I think it was.

ctx.x: Tell me about the first group you had that came to New York and did they pit you against Lucky Millinder’s group?

Oh, yes. See — see at that time Lucky had quite a band and Lucky seemed to be, he was about the most feared group around there. And so they had the number one and number two bandstand and so it was, what they do is I think they start you out on number two and then after you figure you’re pretty good, you think you’re all right, and then they let you go to number one. But anyway though, we had a lot of fun with Lucky. We used to play a half an hour each I think it was. We’d play a half an hour each, half an hour,…

and stuff like that in it. But it wasn’t swinging, you see? So we just kept swinging. And the crowd went for the swing, you know, the crowd went for the swinging. They had that oh the had a heck of a dance group there around New York called, oh I forget. And it looked like the dance group was just made for us and we were made for them, and just everything just worked perfect. But it was a lot of fun though.

items.title: 52193_Jay McShann oral history interview
items.q: when you bring this band to the Savoy for the first time, and meet Lucky Millinder... we opened up with Lucky's band

ctx.x: Lucky I take it had been playing all his best flag wavers and everything.

You know, Lucky, he was quite a showman there was no question about it. He was doing all that stuff, you know what I mean, and the band, playing all them heavy tunes, you know, so after we started going in the books, starting setting them tempos, then the house begin doing this because everybody's going along with the music, so then Lucky, we used to go downstairs and drink, and he was down there at the place, taking a taste, so Lucky's valet went down there and told him, Lucky, you better come upstairs. He said…

Well, I don't know, Lucky, I think you should come up here. I ain't worried about it. Well, Lucky came back up and he went into his books. So when he went into -- so he went down in his books, well, when he did that, then I think that's when we -- we went heavy in the books. And Lucky come back after we went heavy in the books, they clapped about 15 minutes of Lucky's time, so he only got a chance to play 15 minutes, because they clapped and stomped, when he got through
